product.name: Patchback
promise: Get back the patch that plays it.
product.lede: Patchback listens to a recording of a synth note and recovers an editable DSP patch and the note events that drive it. It renders that patch with its own Rust engine, compares the rendering with the recording at several resolutions and refines the patch until it matches. A small regressor trained with ModelSpec proposes where the search starts. No neural audio decoder: what comes out is a program you can open, read and change.
product.meta: One Rust binary · std only, no ML or DSP crates · ModelSpec for training · Apache-2.0

art.caption: Every entity of the Patchback specification and the relations between them, generated from spec/ by patchback-docs.

sections.title: A program, not a waveform.
sections.lede: The output of a fit is a patch file, an events file, a rendering and a report. Every one of them is plain text or a WAV you can inspect.

items.title: An editable patch
items.description: Modules, connections and parameters in physical units: attack in seconds, cutoff in hertz, drive in decibels. Open it, change a value, render it again.

items.title: Rendered by the engine that made the training data
items.description: Training data, previews and the final rendering all come from the same native DSP engine, so a recovered patch always runs.

items.title: A comparison you can read
items.description: Log-spectral, envelope, transient and band-energy terms, each logged for every candidate, after the rendering is aligned with the reference.

items.title: A bounded, seeded search
items.description: Coordinate search over eight normalized parameters within a render budget. The best valid patch is kept; an invalid candidate never replaces it.

items.title: A regressor trained with ModelSpec
items.description: A two-layer network maps 32 audio features to the eight parameters and gives the search its starting point. It is trained on audio Patchback rendered itself.

items.title: Refusals instead of guesses
items.description: An unsupported sample rate, a non-finite sample or an ambiguous pitch is refused with a diagnostic, not converted or estimated silently.

sections.title: Analyze, predict, render, compare, refine.
sections.lede: The regressor only proposes. The rendering and the comparison decide.

steps.label: patchback analyze
steps.title: Analyze
steps.description: Onsets, pitch, envelopes and spectra of the reference; the 32 features of features/1.

steps.label: Regressor
steps.title: Predict
steps.description: Eight normalized parameters from the features, or the default patch when no weights are loaded.

steps.label: patchback render
steps.title: Render
steps.description: The validated patch plays the note events through the native engine at 48 kHz.

steps.label: patchback compare
steps.title: Compare
steps.description: Four loss terms at several resolutions, after time alignment.

steps.label: patchback fit
steps.title: Refine
steps.description: Seeded restarts and coordinate search until the render budget is spent or the gain is too small.
